top_choice_rationale: P001 pairs an identifiable theoretical origin (the Z2 time-reversal-invariant topological insulator and quantum spin Hall proposal of Kane and Mele) with a decisive experiment (helical edge transport in HgTe/CdTe wells by Molenkamp), confirmed for two decades by transport, nonlocal and photoemission measurements, so the discovery is mature and I can evaluate it directly. The allocation has a real gap (Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and the 3D work), but a narrow citation that names the HgTe experiment explicitly keeps the attribution honest, and the 2016 prize concerned quantum Hall and chain physics, not this symmetry class. P002 is a sound, cleanly attributed second choice and clearly better than no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile for P001 (Kane, Mele and Molenkamp are not among my documented connections); for P002 only general academic exchanges with Japan, with no documented tie to Katori or Ye.
